questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I wanted to live in a country where English was the first language and was not very keen on going to the US. Australia therefore seemed like a perfect fit, especially considering the very kind weather climate.
Moreover, the level of law schools in Sydney are generally really good, which of course played a part in my choice of study destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: UNSW was quite good at keeping us informed generally. The individuals responsible for the different courses were less informed regarding the schedule etc., which at times could be frustrating.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We received a tour of the campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Not much orientation, decent information available.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Quite easy if you are willing to spend the same, and maybe a bit more, than you would on rent in Copenhagen. I lived in a very sought after area, and was able to find a rental unit in under 2 days searching.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is expensive if you do not want to live in a sharehouse.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not explore the housing available to students.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: A quite difficult and long process. You have to register for the same courses a couple of times because the enrollment process has a lot of steps. Not hard to get the courses you want though - just tedious and time consuming.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Long Q&A sections at the uni website and very helpful support from designated staff members. A bit hard to reach during their opening hours though when located in Denmark due to the time difference.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a big difference in requirements regarding class participation and exam timetables for the courses available.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Not as challenging as the courses at my home institution.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Quite similar. Courses where held in classes an student participation was encouraged.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
World Religions
Animal Law
International Sports and Relations
Introduction to Australian Legal System

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: World Religions was quite interesting and very different from the courses I have had at my home institution.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Costs of living are pretty much the same in general as in Copenhagen. Beer and wine are however very expensive, so having dinner at a restaurant can be costly. Fruit and vegetables are also pretty expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a lot of clubs etc., but most of them were not very active in term 3, which I took.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of sports clubs, different social gatherings as well.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to social gatherings with both students from Australia as well as other exchange students. That will help gain more of a true Australian social network.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Going on road-trips to different parts of Australia. It is a huge country and there are vast possibilities of exploring all sorts of places from sunny beaches to rain forrest to ski resorts.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Australian culture is very European.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: UNSW did not have the best socializing options for exchange students to meet with local students. So I would say take any opportunity you can to meet local students, also from other universities.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing much really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Australians are very outgoing and helpful, so it did not feel as a burden to ask strangers for help etc. Very easy to meet new friends outside of uni as well.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Plan your courses if you want to have a lot of free time to do road-trips etc., practice your written English as a lot of the work is done in writing, do not do student housing.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The many friends I met from Australia and to experience living abroad.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The time difference compared with Denmark can be quite brutal, but it is manageable to stay in touch with friends and family.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
